title: Module 8 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: Two groups of 8 have M1 = 24 (s = 6) and M2 = 19 (s = 5). What is the pooled variance?
What is the estimated standard error of the difference?
items.why: The square root of (30.5/8 + 30.5/8) = the square root of 7.625 = 2.76.

items.q: What is the independent-measures t, and the degrees of freedom?
items.why: t = (24 minus 19)/2.76 = 1.81, and df = 8 + 8 minus 2 = 14. The critical t at .05 two-tailed is 2.145, so the result is not significant.

items.q: Cohen's d, using the pooled SD, is about
items.why: d = 5 divided by the square root of 30.5 (5.52) = .905. A large effect that the small groups cannot confirm.

items.q: A researcher says, "Because my groups were not significantly different, they must have had equal means." What is wrong?
o: The sample means differed by 5. The test only shows the difference is not distinguishable from sampling error
The groups should have been larger
The mean difference is the standard error
items.why: Non-significance concerns the population. The sample means still differ, and the data are compatible with a real difference.
